title: Compact Quickstart Hero & Micro-Journey Assets with Screenshot Pipeline
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Replace the current wide-hero quickstart on the landing page with a compact, scannable hero and a set of micro-journey tiles that lead into the quickstart flows. Deliver a production-ready Figma component library, a screenshot generation pipeline for release screenshots, and a dev handoff packet with responsive breakpoints and motion-reduced variants.

Scope: Hero layout (compact left-aligned content + right visual), three micro-journey tiles (Start, Integrate, Deploy), step-by-step inline visuals for each tile, updated product screenshots captured with the new pipeline, and lightweight motion for hero transitions. Must support English and European locales (EN, FR, DE) in this phase.

Success metrics: 1) 10% increase in quickstart CTA clickthrough in the experiment cohort; 2) 30% reduction in time-to-first-screenshot for release assets (automation); 3) no accessibility regressions (contrast and reduced motion).

Constraints: Must fit within existing console header and not require additional backend endpoints. Screenshot pipeline must produce 3 responsive variants (desktop 1200px, tablet 768px, mobile 375px) and export to WebP + PNG. Maintain tokenized component styles to align with theme tokens in the design system.

Deliverables: Figma library file with components and variants, JSON style token spec for engineering, automated screenshot script and README in the webapp repo, annotated Zeplin-like spec (in Confluence) for spacing and copy, QA checklist, and A/B test specification for Growth.
acceptance_criteria: Figma components built with responsive variants and export slices for required breakpoints
Automated screenshot script produces WebP and PNG outputs and is documented in the repo README
Design tokens and spacing documented and match theme tokens used by webapp/style guide
Motion has a reduced-motion fallback state and meets WCAG contrast ratios
Handoff ticket includes example copy, ARIA guidance, and test cases for QA
tasks: Create micro-journey tiles with 3 step illustrations each
Build Figma components and variants, publish library
Implement screenshot automation script and CI hook
Run accessibility review and adjust contrast and focus order
Prepare dev handoff packet and attend handoff session
Coordinate with PM for A/B experiment runway and metrics
decisions: Use compact left-text with right visual layout to preserve content density and improve scan time
Replace long paragraph copy with 3 micro-journey CTAs to reduce cognitive load
Use static PNG fallbacks for emails and social while using WebP on the site
Motion will be a single crossfade + subtle translate; QA must include prefers-reduced-motion behavior
tradeoffs: Choosing compact hero reduces opportunity for large hero illustration but improves mobile density
Automated screenshot pipeline adds CI complexity but saves manual capture time per release
Supporting three locales now limits ability to localize image text; we will avoid embedded text where possible
